elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 expressly provides that the Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: The designated forum includes the state courts located in New York County, New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 expressly designates the state courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: The designated forum includes the federal courts located in New York County, New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 expressly designates the federal courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: Jurisdiction of the designated New York County state and federal courts is exclusive.
elements.evidence: Although Section 28.2 states that those courts have exclusive jurisdiction, it permits either Party to seek temporary injunctive relief in another court concerning confidential information or intellectual property. This express exception prevents jurisdiction from being fully exclusive.

elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 selects New York law, not any of the permitted fallback laws.

elements.element: The designated courts are Delaware courts, California courts, or the courts of London, corresponding to the selected fallback law.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 designates state and federal courts in New York County rather than Delaware courts, California courts, or London courts.

result.reason: The redline correctly selects New York law and New York County state and federal courts, but the express temporary-injunctive-relief carveout permits proceedings in other courts and therefore does not meet the preferred requirement of exclusive New York County jurisdiction. It also does not satisfy the separate fallback because neither the selected law nor forum is a fallback option. The drafting is otherwise clear and removes the prior Singapore-law/New York-forum mismatch without disturbing unrelated terms.
